assembly_notes: Bi-fold closet door system. The grounded `opening_frame` part lines the opening: two side jambs, a sill, a header and a CadQuery U-track whose web and two downward lips leave a real open channel, plus one mullion post per extra pair. Each of bifold_pair_count bays carries a `pivot_leaf` on a REVOLUTE (+z) jamb or mullion pivot followed by fold_set's remaining leaves on REVOLUTE (+z) centre hinges. Every centre hinge MIMICS the bay's own jamb joint, alternating -2.0 and +2.0 down the chain, so a pair folds face to face and a trifold folds as a real accordion; either way the bay keeps one honest degree of freedom and can never be posed into an impossible fold. The knuckle stand-off flips side at each centre hinge, which is what lets successive leaves swing apart instead of closing onto each other. The roller or guide pin that rides the header channel is carried by the handle leaf itself. leaf_face changes only what the leaf field is made of - a plain slab, a framed reflective insert, pitched louver slats, raised centre fields or a framed glass lite - and every candidate keeps the same stile, rail and hinge edges. hardware_set changes how the inner leaf is carried: a floor pivot pin with a track roller, knuckled butt hinges on the jamb face, a top-hung carrier with a slim floor locating pin, a dual-track set whose second guide runs in the sill under a floor roller, or full-height heavy pivots that carry the whole leaf on stout corner plates with no roller at all. opening_width_m, opening_height_m and closet_depth_m are honest continuous parameters that derive bay width, leaf span and height, track length, hinge spacing and the fold envelope; palette, slat count and panel bevels are non-core.  The leaves that swing each way have to cancel, or the free edge would walk out of the header channel as the set folds: a pair does that with two equal halves, and the accordion needs its middle leaf as wide as the two outer ones together, so trifold bays are proportioned narrow-wide-narrow.
